title: orient arg schema fights agent intuition (path/query/scope footguns)
description:
orient requires BOTH `workspace` and `scope`, and `scope` must resolve to a component name/id or a file path — not `.`, not `repo`, not a free-text query. Agents intuit orient as "point at a repo/area and get oriented" and pass path/query/./repo, all of which error. The signature doesn't match the mental model, which is a large part of why orient is called 7 times ever.

CANDIDATE FIX: accept `.`/repo/omitted scope as a whole-workspace overview; accept `path` as a `workspace` alias; and/or make scope optional. Align the tool to how agents actually reach for it.

GATED on sutra/312: only worth doing if orient is kept (realign path). If deleted, close wontfix.
reproduction: History (~/.claude): of 7 orient calls, 3 failed on arg shape — agent passed `query=...` (like explore), passed `path=...` instead of `workspace=`, or omitted `scope`; 1 more passed scope=`.`/`repo` → "no component found matching scope".

messages.author: user
messages.text: wontfix — superseded by sutra/312 (delete orient). Arg-schema footgun is moot once the tool is gone. Negative knowledge: orient required BOTH workspace and scope, with scope resolving only to a component name/id or file path (not path/query/./repo). That mismatch with how agents reach for a "orient me on this area" tool drove ~half its few invocations to error. Lesson for any future scoped tool: make the arg shape match the reach — accept a bare path / whole-workspace default, not a mandatory component handle.
